comments.body:
Investigation + production repair (2026-11-11, PST).

Observation (prod clone /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets, git 2.47.3 in the MCP container):
- Before: 78,737 loose objects (~9.7 GB loose on disk), 235 packs, 2.27 GB packed; commit-graph last written 2026-08-31.
- `.git/objects/maintenance.lock` and `.git/gc.pid` both dated 2026-09-03 01:36:18 UTC (2026-09-02 18:36 PDT) — stranded since then. 12 `fetch-pack` `.keep` files from 2026-09-05..09-15 (killed fetches).
- Reproduced in the prod container on git 2.47.3 (scratch repo): with a maintenance.lock present, `git maintenance run --auto` exits 0 and does nothing; removing it makes the same command pack. Upstream git never expires maintenance.lock (confirmed in upstream patch thread + several downstream reports).
- rebar's deferred step `run_auto_maintenance` runs exactly `git maintenance run --auto`, so every write since 2026-09-03 got a silent no-op.
- Live, within ~30 s of removing the stale lock: rebar-mcp (container PID 1) adopted an ORPHANED `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --no-detach` -> `gc --auto` -> `repack --cruft` + `prune`, running outside rebar's write lock (I was holding it). Its parent was a git porcelain process that had already died. Locally confirmed: `git fetch` and `git merge` each spawn `git maintenance run --auto` as a child; rebar suppresses that only on commits (`_AUTOMAINT_OFF`), not on sync/push fetch (30 s bound) or merge (120 s bound).
- A full repack of this store took 605.6 s and 2.58 GB RSS. It cannot finish under either bound.

Repair (operator-authorized prod write), under rebar's own `write_lock` in a one-off container from the same image (no cgroup cap):
- Backup: `cp -a .git` -> `/var/lib/rebar/backups/mcp-tickets-gitdir-20261111T192528Z` (12 GB; `git rev-parse --git-dir` resolves to the copy; all 3 refs identical to live). It is a standalone gitdir, not a worktree pointer.
- Removed the stranded maintenance.lock, gc.pid and the 12 stale `.keep` files; `git repack -a -d -l` (605.6 s). I deliberately aborted my own `prune --expire=now` (fetches run outside the write lock, so expire=now could race a fetch's fresh loose objects); the orphaned gc then ran git's own `prune --expire 2.weeks.ago` and rewrote commit-graph.
- After: 10 loose objects, 2 packs (1 + cruft), 1.1 GB objects dir. Refs unchanged.
- History walk timings (3 runs each, same commands): `git log -- <ticket-dir>` 104.9/116.6/113.4 s -> 28.4/23.2/23.4 s; `git log --name-only -n 5000` 32.5/25.5/21.0 s -> 4.1/3.0/3.1 s; `rev-list --count HEAD` ~0.9 s -> ~0.55 s. fsck connectivity check pending.

Next: durable code fix in progress (worktree fix-gonolek).

HANDOFF STATE (2026-11-11 16:20 PST, session 3d705fec)

**Status:** CLOSED through the completion gate, class `preexisting`. All 3 acceptance-criteria boxes are ticked. AC2 and AC3 are tagged `[non-codebase]` with provenance lines, validated by `provenance_gaps`.

**Root cause, with evidence:**
- On 2026-09-03 01:36:18 UTC, a stranded `objects/maintenance.lock` was left behind. Git never expires that lock, and while it exists, `git maintenance run --auto` exits 0 and does nothing. This was reproduced on git 2.47.3 inside the container. rebar's explicit post-write step was therefore a silent no-op for about 10 weeks.
- How the lock was stranded:
  - `git fetch` and `git merge` start a foreground `maintenance run --auto` themselves. rebar suppressed this on commits but not on bounded sync/push fetches or merges.
  - On this store that run is a full gc: a full repack took 605.6 s, and `gc --auto` took 133.9 s. A rebar timeout SIGKILLs only the parent, so the orphaned gc kept running outside the write lock. This was observed live, adopted by the container's PID 1.
  - A hard kill during that run left the lock in place.

**Production repair (11:25–11:39 PST):**
- Backed up the gitdir to `/var/lib/rebar/backups/mcp-tickets-gitdir-20261111T192528Z` (12 GB, standalone; refs verified identical).
- Under rebar's write lock: removed the stale lock, `gc.pid` and 12 stale `.keep` files, then ran `repack -a -d -l`.
- `fsck --connectivity-only` exited 0, and refs were unchanged.
- The backup is still on disk; delete it at the operator's discretion. The root disk is 55% used.

**Before and after:**

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Loose objects | 78,737 | 4–336 in steady state |
| Packs | 235 | 2–4 |
| Store-wide position walk | 427.5 s | 220–232 s (limit 300 s) |
| Per-ticket path walk | 105–117 s | 23–28 s |
| `log --name-only -n 5000` | 21–33 s | 2.9–4.1 s |

**Durable fix:**
- Gerrit change 3351, merged as 334295da063a5840f17d689583337dbbd1587a33. It is deployed in release 0.15.1, container image aa1e294.
- Bounded git children carry `maintenance.auto=false` and `gc.auto=0`, as does the container's start-up fetch.
- The explicit step runs only the incremental tasks: commit-graph, loose-objects and incremental-repack.
- A timed-out step is reaped as a process group, SIGTERM first.
- No config key, env var or flag was added, and there is no `mechanism-ok` marker.

**Follow-up bugs (all linked discovered_from):**
- `saccharine-unwise-barnacle`: recover from a stale `maintenance.lock`. Needs a lock-mechanism decision.
- `idle-ammoniacal-axisdeer`: group-reap the other bounded git calls, which leave `.keep` files and orphaned children.
- `successive-deceptive-xiphias`: no path now prunes unreachable objects or expires reflogs; two docs are stale.

**Pending decisions:** none for this ticket.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation (read-only, production MCP host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, 2026-11-05)

The production MCP tickets clone (`/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, container label `rebar.service=mcp`) has received no git object maintenance since early September:

- `git count-objects -v`: 74,605 loose objects (8.63 GiB loose), 235 packs (2.16 GiB), 306,528 commits.
- `.git/objects/info/commit-graph` dated 2026-08-31; `objects/info/packs` dated 2026-09-02.
- Local operator checkout of the same history: 6 packs, 333 MiB loose, current commit-graph chain.

History walks there are much slower than on a clone of the same history:

| walk (same command as rebar.attest.authorship_resolution) | production (shared clone in the container) | operator clone |
|---|---|---|
| store-wide `build_position_commit_map` (`-- '*.json'`) | 427.5 s | 111 s (bug breezelike-travelsick-moray, 2026-11-03 comment) |
| per-ticket map, 26a0-0104-9b63-4500 | 160.8 s | 19.1 s |
| per-ticket map, fb16-a8b0-c2b7-449a | 266.1 s | not measured |

The store-wide walk exceeds its 300 s timeout in production, so the compaction sweep's shared position map is always `None` there and every fold falls back to a per-ticket walk. Bug breezelike-travelsick-moray moves that walk outside the store write lock; it does not make the walk faster, so a production sweep still spends minutes per ticket before each fold.

Store commits run with automatic maintenance disabled (`_AUTOMAINT_OFF` in compact.py and the commit seam), and `gc.autodetach=false`, `maintenance.autodetach=false` are set on the clone. Unverified: which component, if any, is meant to repack or rewrite the commit-graph on the production clone, and whether the 2 vCPU host or the 3.6 GiB container memory cap also contribute.

## Expected

The production tickets clone's object store stays packed with a current commit-graph, so path-limited history walks cost about what they cost on a fresh clone, and the store-wide position walk finishes inside its timeout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The mechanism that should keep the production tickets clone packed (or its absence) is identified with evidence.
- [x] [non-codebase] After the fix, production `git count-objects -v` shows loose objects bounded and the commit-graph current, measured read-only via SSM.
  provenance: environment=production MCP host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, containers rebar-mcp-334295da063a-8092 and rebar-mcp-aa1e294069a5-8093 on the shared tickets clone; principal=AWS SSM RunCommand under the operator's frontier profile, executing as the instance role; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the measurement is a read-only git command run inside the live production container, so it only exists in production and cannot be reproduced from the repository.
- [x] [non-codebase] The store-wide position walk completes inside its 300 s timeout in production, measured on a shared clone in the container.
  provenance: environment=production MCP host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, container rebar-mcp-aa1e294069a5-8093 (release 0.15.1, contains the fix) on the shared tickets clone; principal=AWS SSM RunCommand under the operator's frontier profile, executing as the instance role; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the measurement is a read-only git command run inside the live production container, so it only exists in production and cannot be reproduced from the repository.
